note: Tally.Lower takes an argument named `count` — the same name as the tally's field — and its given reads `count.value < 0`. Per C2.2 a bare name resolves against the command's arguments first, so with the stored count at 10 a Lower by -3 is accepted (the argument -3 is negative) and a Lower by 4 is refused GivenNotMet (the argument 4 is not). Under state-first resolution (C2.3, an ensures' rule) the stored 10 would have been read and the first Lower refused. The other half of C2.2, an unknown head being an evaluation fault, needs a malformed domain and is not reachable through dispatch.
